subject: Next steps & model recommendations — DatumSearch semantic pilot
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Paul Dixon <pdixon@datumsearch.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & model recommendations — DatumSearch semantic pilot

Hi Paul — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a small evaluation with your team.

Recap (short):
- Use case: semantic search over product docs + support tickets (initial index ~50k docs, eventual growth expected ~500k).
- Success metrics mentioned: recall@10 for top-k retrieval, MRR, and false-positive rate on named-entity-sensitive queries. Also care about embedding dimensionality impact on indexing cost.
- Security: you asked about private deployment options (VPC + KMS) and SOC 2 evidence.

Recommended models for pilot (quick picks):
1) redwood-embed-v2 (baseline): 1536-d dense embeddings, strong recall@10 on our retail/support benchmarks.
2) open-embed-lite-8bit (cost-optimized): 1024-d quantized option for lower unit cost; expect slight recall delta but better index size.
3) redwood-embed-hybrid (sparse + dense) — experimental: useful if you want aggressive recall at low latency (adds index complexity).

Benchmarks & artifacts attached:
- embed_benchmarks_datasearch.csv (sampleed from similar customers)
- datasearch_seed_prompts_v1.txt (recommended prompt sets for human evaluation / relevance labeling)

Concerns to watch (from our side):
- Dimensionality tradeoffs: 1536 vs 1024 dims — index storage, ANN recall, and drift sensitivity differ; we'll run both and report normalized recall per GB.
- Quantization impact: 8-bit runs well but we measure nearest-neighbor rank shifts on tail (low-frequency entities).
- Drift monitoring: we'll include simple drift checks (cosine distribution shift + embedding centroid drift) and set alert thresholds.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a 10k sample (anonymized) S3 bucket or secure upload link.
2) We run a 48–72 hour baseline evaluation (redwood-embed-v2 + open-embed-lite-8bit) that calculates recall@1/5/10, MRR, and false-positive examples.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive for ingestion and security (I propose Wed May 5, 10:00am PT).
4) If results look good, scope a 10-business-day pilot for full 50k index + monitoring.

Logistics & security:
- We can accept data via presigned S3, or via your SFTP; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS.
- SOC 2 report & limited-scope encryption docs attached upon NDA — happy to route to your security team.

Can you confirm availability for the May 5th deep-dive and the preferred upload method for the sample? If you want, I can also attach an initial pilot proposal (short) — marked as attached.

Thanks — looking forward to running the eval.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: datasearch_seed_prompts_v1.txt (text), embed_benchmarks_datasearch.csv (csv), pilot-proposal-datumsearch.pdf (pdf)

From: Paul Dixon <pdixon@datumsearch.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & model recommendations — DatumSearch semantic pilot

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying Qs so we can expedite: 

1) Drift & dimensionality: do you have a recommended threshold or heuristic for centroid drift vs cosine-distribution shifts we should watch for on initial runs? We see seasonal vocabulary shifts in support tickets.

2) Quantization question: will the 8-bit variant materially change nearest-neighbor ordering for tail queries (low-occurrence SKUs)? If so, we need to be careful about surface-area exposed to customers.

3) Security: we definitely need SOC 2 evidence and prefer presigned S3. Can you confirm if presigned S3 + server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) satisfies your upload path?

4) Sample size: 10k is OK to start; can we do 12k to include more recent tickets? We can deliver as gzipped newline-delimited JSON.

If you can run the 48–72h baseline on 12k this week, that would help our internal prioritization. Also looping in Lina from security (lina@datumbreach.com) — she'll pipe in if she needs anything.

Thanks — Paul
Paul Dixon
Head of Search, DatumSearch
pdixon@datumsearch.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T20:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & model recommendations — DatumSearch semantic pilot (internal)

Looping in internal plan and owners — internal notes below.

Vanessa / Marissa — can one of you confirm capacity to run the baseline on 12k (Paul asked for 12k vs 10k)? Proposed assignment: Marissa owns the eval runs and metrics, Rishi will provision the sandbox and handle security checklist.

Proposed quick timeline:
- Provision sandbox + presigned S3 ingestion (Rishi): 4–6 hours once I open infra ticket.
- Baseline eval (Marissa): 48–72 hours once data available. Runs: redwood-embed-v2 (1536) and open-embed-lite-8bit (1024). We'll produce recall@1/5/10, MRR, per-class coverage and a small set of failure-case examples.
- Deliverable: one-page executive summary + detailed bench CSV (same format as attached), and set of visualizations showing cosine distribution shift and dimensionality cost per GB.

HubSpot: I'll update DS-3421 with this plan and set the stage for pilot proposal. Pilot proposal draft attached (pilot-proposal-datumsearch.pdf).

Marissa — can you start a job and reserve GPU slots for Thursday morning if Paul gives us the data by tomorrow afternoon?

Rishi

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Paul Dixon <pdixon@datumsearch.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & model recommendations — DatumSearch semantic pilot

Paul — great, confirmed on the 12k sample. We can accept gzipped NDJSON via presigned S3 with SSE-KMS. Rishi will provision the bucket and share a presigned upload link by EOD today.

On your questions:
- Drift heuristic: we'll compute centroid distance + KL-style shift over cosine bins. Initial trigger threshold: centroid shift > 0.12 (cosine units) OR 20% increase in low-confidence queries (you can treat those as cos_sim < 0.22). We will tune thresholds after the baseline.
- Quantization / tail impact: from prior customers we see a 2–5% drop in recall@1 for very low-frequency entities with 8-bit. We'll surface failure cases so you can decide whether to use quantized in prod.
- SOC 2: happy to share the report after NDA; presigned S3 + SSE-KMS is an accepted path.

Next steps (action items):
1) Paul: confirm final sample delivery format (gzipped NDJSON ok?) and drop ETA.
2) Rishi: create presigned S3 + share link; add security checklist items to HubSpot DS-3421.
3) Marissa: standby to run eval once upload completes; reserve Thursday GPU window.
4) Paul: confirm tech deep-dive — Wed May 5, 10:00am PT works for us; we'll send a calendar invite.

We aim to have baseline results ready within 72 hours after upload. If you want a one-page results summary for execs, we'll include that with highlights and a recommended production configuration (index size + cost estimate).

Thanks — talk soon.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
